articles.title: ‘Very weak. Very bad’: how Rodri’s verdict exposed woeful Valencia’s crisis | Sid Lowe
articles.summary: The World Cup winner’s off-the-cuff assessment was brutally honest. Within days their manager and CEO were gone, but the problems run much deeper. Kiat Lim wanted to see Valencia play so badly, so that is what he did.
body: Above him as he went in were giant portraits of Mario Kempes, Antonio Puchades, Juan Sol, Gaizka Mendieta, David Villa and Santiago Cañizares, footballers from a better time; around him were yellow banners and whistles for the footballers there now. Inside, Lim saw the game start with the lower south stand empty as fans stayed away until the 19th minute, the sound of another protest drifting in from the street. They were out there still when, sitting alongside Joan Laporta, he saw Lamine Yamal score the sixth-minute opener then get a second. And although that, also from Lamine Yamal, was ruled out, he eventually saw Barcelona get four more, presiding over a 5-0 debut defeat.

He had seen supporters leave early, seen those that stayed turn towards him, chanting for him and his family to leave for good. He had seen the hankies come out and his players head into the tunnel heads bowed. He heard his manager insist that they were hurt but not sunk. What he did not see – what no one had seen yet but everyone would see soon enough – was the verdict from the bench.

articles.title: Andoni Iraola says Liverpool took ‘a step backwards’ in draw against Fulham
articles.summary: Head coach insists forwards need to improve pressing. Changes up front likely for Carabao Cup tie against Spurs. Andoni Iraola has shifted the focus on to Liverpool’s forwards for the team’s uninspiring display against Fulham, insisting they need to give more to make his system work.
body: The head coach admitted his team took “a step backwards” with their goalless draw on Saturday. His central midfield pairing of Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai struggled to contain their Fulham counterparts, winning two of five duels and one of nine duels respectively. But Iraola believes the problems started further forward with the pressing of Liverpool’s expensively assembled attack.

“It’s not a matter of just the midfielders,” he said. “When we have been good collectively the midfielders have looked a lot better and recovered more balls. It’s not because they are winning duels that they play better, it’s because we are helping them more to win the duels.

“If the ones up front do their job very well then the defenders and midfielders look good. If we are allowing them to defend one-v-one all the time and we are not aggressive, then our defenders will also struggle. If the players ahead of you are doing their job then you look a better midfielder or defender because you win more easier duels, you have more chance of winning one. It is more collective.

articles.title: No weekend game for Manchester derby VAR officials
articles.summary: The video assistant referee for the Manchester derby, Matt Donohue, and his assistant VAR, Blake Antrobus, are not appointed for this weekend's Premier League games.
body: The decision was made by the Premier League refereeing body Pro Ref's chief refereeing officer Howard Webb and the management team.
It follows Pro Ref admitting to an "error of judgement" in awarding Erling Haaland's winning goal for Manchester City at Manchester United on Sunday.
The striker scored in the 60th minute at Old Trafford when he turned in a shot at the back post from Josko Gvardiol's cross.
His effort was initially disallowed on the field for offside but, following VAR intervention, the goal was awarded as the Norwegian was ruled to have been played onside by Patrick Dorgu's boot.

articles.title: VARs who wrongly confirmed Haaland’s goal at Manchester United are stood down
articles.summary: Matt Donohue and his assistant not used this weekend. Pro Ref said allowing winner was ‘error of judgment’ The video assistant referee officials who allowed Erling Haaland’s winning goal in the Manchester derby on Sunday have been stood down.
body: The chief refereeing officer, Howard Webb, took the decision with his management team after a review of the weekend’s action. Their availability will be reconsidered after the international break.

Donohoe was called on to check Michael Oliver’s decision to disallow Haaland’s 60th-minute goal for offside. Using semi-automated offside technology, Donohoe was able to establish that the Manchester City striker was onside and overturned Oliver’s call. However, he failed to spot Enzo Fernández had influenced play from an offside position, an infringement Pro Ref said should have led him to recommend an on-field review.

This is the first time officials have been made to stand down this season owing to an error. Donohoe, an EFL referee since 2018, has taken charge of three Championship matches this season as well as his VAR work. His EFL profile says he has completed Pro Ref’s “Enhanced VAR Training Programme”. Antrobus is also an assistant referee in the Premier League and ran the line in the first three matchdays.

articles.title: England give Fleming unprecedented consent to balance job with TV role in New Zealand
articles.summary: Test coach to work for Sky NZ in October and December. Fleming will plan South Africa tour in upcoming weeks. England’s new Test head coach Stephen Fleming will return to New Zealand to work as a commentator on the Black Caps’ Test and white ball series against India next month despite having…
body: Fleming arrived in England on Monday for a 10-day trip which will feature talks with the captain Joe Root and the England and Wales Cricket Board’s (ECB) managing director of men’s cricket, Rob Key, after missing this summer’s three-Test series against Pakistan with the batting coach, Marcus Trescothick, presiding over a 3-0 win.

The ECB granted Fleming a late start date after confirming his appointment in late July as the former New Zealand captain had requested the opportunity to spend time with his family after ending a 17-year run coaching the Chennai Super Kings this summer. The board has been similarly flexible in accommodating his commentary work.

Sky New Zealand, which has no connection to the UK broadcaster Sky Sports that has exclusive rights to England’s home matches, announced on Monday that Fleming will be part of its commentary team for the India tour which comprises two Tests, five one-day internationals and five T20s running between 22 October and 1 December.

articles.title: Does derby semi add 'more spice' or simply 'nice for fans'?
articles.summary: While Hibernian head coach David Gray is relishing a "very special" Premier Sports Cup semi-final against Heart of Midlothian, counterpart Wouter Vrancken is keeping cool about the prospect.
body: David Gray and Wouter Vrancken's reaction to Hibernian and Heart of Midlothian being drawn together in the Premier Sports Cup semi-final could hardly be more contrasting.

For Gray, a veteran of Edinburgh derbies as a player and head coach, not forgetting his winning goal for Hibs in the 2016 Scottish Cup final against Rangers, it is "a brilliant opportunity" and one that has "a bit more spice to it" because of the opposition.
For Vrancken, who joined Hearts from his hometown club of Sint-Truiden this summer, it will simply be "nice for the fans" to be facing their bitter rivals.
It will be interesting to hear the Belgian's thoughts once he has experienced his first trip to Hampden Park - and a first-ever League Cup semi-final between the sides.

articles.title: Bremer spoke with Juventus stars to convince them to stay this season
articles.summary: Gleison Bremer is one of the best players at Juventus, and he is also one of the leaders in the Bianconeri dressing room. As a result, he is highly respected by his teammates and is using that influence to good effect.
body: The defender has now revealed that he spoke to Douglas Luiz and Nicolas Gonzalez about staying at the club during the summer, when both players were expected to leave.

Juventus had been open to both players leaving for the right price, after they spent last season on loan at different clubs. The Bianconeri were prepared for the possibility of losing them and believed they could still perform well if the departures happened.

Gonzalez did not want to play for Juventus again, while Luiz was open to leaving if an offer arrived. However, the Brazilian became more open to remaining after none of his loan clubs completed a permanent deal for him.

Luiz now wants stability and an opportunity to prove that he can perform well in Turin. Meanwhile, Gonzalez was forced to remain at Juventus because there was no serious offer for his signature during the last transfer window.

The two newcomers slot in at No. 8 and No.

articles.title: Brundle: Debating the rule that cost Norris and why Madring needs changes
articles.summary: The inaugural Madring grand prix was ok, the new venue offering some interesting aspects such as the long and banked turn 12 and testing high-speed sections between continuous and unrelenting walls and barriers.
body: It all had a feeling of work in progress. We know they lost a lot of time in the build process with particularly bad weather, and as a temporary race track adjacent to the international airport, and effectively racing around the Madrid equivalent of the Birmingham NEC, it had its challenges.
The pitlane and paddock were simply vast, creating some logistical challenges for all and, much more importantly, the track layout was not conducive to overtaking, to say the least.

As the cars swung at high speed from side to side through some of the more tortuous sections, and with a reasonably fast corner onto the not especially long pit straight, along with an energy dense layout meaning hybrid batteries would be replenished far more easily than on the four high speed and long straights just a week earlier in Monza, the only way to overtake was a highly risky lunge, or wait for rivals to make a mistake.

It's not as challenging to overtake as Monaco, but not that far short either. Given the extremely long pit lane which feeds back onto the inside of turn three, it took a lengthy 25 seconds to pit under green-flag conditions.

articles.title: Max Verstappen admits he ‘seriously considered’ quitting F1 before signing new Red Bull contract
articles.summary: Max Verstappen has admitted he came close to stepping away from Formula 1 before extending his deal with Red Bull last month, despite holding discussions with rival teams.
body: Speaking to German publication Bild after agreeing a deal until 2030, the four-time world champion discussed retirement thoughts and confirmed talks took place with McLaren.
"You have to take every conversation with another team seriously," Verstappen said. "But in the end, I was closer to quitting Formula 1 than to signing with another racing team."
"You either quit or you don't, so it's a 50/50 decision," he added. "I seriously considered calling it quits. But at the end of the day, I just love racing."

The 28-year-old won four consecutive F1 titles from 2021 to 2024, but remains winless this season. He sits sixth in the standings following Sunday's runner-up finish at the Spanish Grand Prix in Madrid, 147 points adrift of Mercedes leader Kimi Antonelli.
